Your strawberry frosting containing FD&C Red No. 3 must stop being manufactured with that color additive by January 15, 2027. On that date, the removal of 21 CFR 74.303 (the listing authorizing FD&C Red No. 3 in food) takes effect, and all existing certificates for batches of FD&C Red No. 3 cease to be effective for use in food (90 FR 4628; 91 FR 50475). Regarding product already on shelves: The January 2025 order explicitly states that '[w]hen FD&C Red No. 3 has been used in food or ingested drugs while its certificate is still effective, such food or ingested drugs will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use of such color additive' (90 FR 4628). This means frosting manufactured and containing FD&C Red No. 3 that was incorporated while the certificate was still effective (i.e., before January 15, 2027) is NOT adulterated and may remain on shelves and be sold after that date. Only use of FD&C Red No. 3 after its certificate ceases to be effective (i.e., incorporating it into food on or after January 15, 2027) would render the food adulterated.

response.answer: Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify through one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient whole foods or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to use the 'healthy' claim: (1) **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement**: The food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups that are the foundation of a healthy dietary pattern (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free or low-fat dairy, lean meat, seafood, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, nuts, or seeds), as defined in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3). (2) **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement**: The food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients. These limits vary by food category (individual foods, mixed products, main dishes, meals) as set forth in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v). This two-pronged approach is confirmed in the background summary of the rule: the food must 'meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients' (90 FR 10592, document 2025-03118, Section II Background). The compliance date for these requirements is February 25, 2028 (89 FR 106064).

response.answer: The 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim is governed by 21 CFR 101.65(d). This section defines the general nutritional claims paragraph that covers labeling claims using the term 'healthy' or related terms as implied nutrient content claims because they suggest that a food may help consumers maintain healthy dietary practices due to its nutrient content. The general principles for nutrient content claims (including the definition of implied nutrient content claims) are set forth in 21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii), which specifically identifies 'healthy' as an example of an implied nutrient content claim that 'suggests that a food, because of its nutrient content, may be useful in maintaining healthy dietary practices' (21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii), as amended by 89 FR 106064). The final rule updating the definition of 'healthy' was published on 2024-12-27 (89 FR 106064, Doc. 2024-29957), with an effective date of 2025-04-28 (as revised by Doc. 2025-03118) and a compliance date of 2028-02-25.

response.answer:
No, that was not a fair reading in mid-2025, and it is definitively incorrect now.

**What was true in mid-2025:** The January 2025 order revoking FD&C Red No. 3 (90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16, Doc. 2025-00830) was subject to an automatic administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) as of February 18, 2025, triggered by the filing of objections. During that stay, the effective dates of January 15, 2027 (food uses, removal of 21 CFR 74.303) and January 18, 2028 (ingested drugs, removal of 21 CFR 74.1303) were suspended pending FDA's resolution of the objections. However, the order itself was a final binding order — not a proposal — and the stay was a procedural pause, not a substantive reversal. The stay did not change the stated effective dates; it merely suspended their operation temporarily. Saying the removal was 'not final and might never take effect' overstated the situation: the order was final on its face, and the stay would end once FDA acted on the objections.

**What is the position now:** FDA published a final document on August 5, 2026 (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920) that (1) overruled all objections, (2) denied requests for a public hearing, (3) lifted the administrative stay as of August 5, 2026, and (4) confirmed the original effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028. The document states: 'we are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, respectively' (91 FR 50475). This constitutes 'final action on the objections' under section 701(e)(2) of the FD&C Act.

The revocation is therefore fully confirmed and binding. The operative deadline for food uses (removal of 21 CFR 74.303) is January 15, 2027 — derived from the effective date, as no separate compliance date was stated. After that date, use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food will render the food adulterated (90 FR 4628). For ingested drugs (removal of 21 CFR 74.1303), the deadline is January 18, 2028.

response.answer:
The order published at 90 FR 4628 (Doc. 2025-00830, published January 16, 2025) changes three CFR provisions within 21 CFR Part 74, and they do NOT all change on the same day. The amendatory instructions are:

1. **Amendatory Instruction 2 – Remove 21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use). This removes the entire listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 as a color additive in food (including dietary supplements). Effective date: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

2. **Amendatory Instruction 3 – Revise 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). Because § 74.1303 currently cross-references the identity and specifications in § 74.303(a)(1) and (b), the order revises § 74.1303 to incorporate that information directly so it can stand alone after § 74.303 is removed. This revision takes effect on the same date as the removal of § 74.303: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628 at preamble section VI; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

3. **Amendatory Instruction 4 – Remove 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). This removes the listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs. Effective date: **January 18, 2028** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

Thus, the provisions do NOT all change on the same day. The food-related changes (removal of § 74.303 and interim revision of § 74.1303) take effect January 15, 2027, while the final removal of § 74.1303 (ingested drugs) takes effect January 18, 2028.

The order was subject to an administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) from February 18, 2025, through August 5, 2026, but that stay has been lifted and the original effective dates are confirmed without change (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920). No separate compliance date is stated; the operative deadlines are derived from the effective dates—after each effective date, use of FD&C Red No. 3 renders the relevant product adulterated (90 FR 4628 at preamble section VI).

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This carve-out means that a food bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d) is not required to include the § 101.13(h) disclosure statement, even if the food would otherwise trigger it. All other provisions of § 101.13 (e.g., type size requirements in § 101.13(f), the general definition of nutrient content claims in § 101.13(b), and other general principles) remain applicable to a 'healthy' claim.

response.answer: Yes, your shelf-stable lentil soup labeled 'healthy' is affected by the updated definition of the term 'healthy' under the final rule published at 89 FR 106064 (Doc. 2024-29957, published 2024-12-27). This rule revises 21 CFR 101.65(d) to establish new food-group-equivalent (FGE) and nutrient-to-limit (NTL) criteria for foods bearing the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim. Under the new framework, your lentil soup would need to qualify under one of the pathways in § 101.65(d)(3): either as a food comprised solely of qualifying ingredients with no other added ingredients except water (paragraph (d)(3)(i), which lists beans, peas, and lentils among qualifying foods), or as a mixed product meeting the FGE and NTL requirements in paragraph (d)(3)(iii), depending on its formulation. If your soup contains added ingredients beyond water and the listed foundational foods (e.g., salt, oil, seasonings), it would not qualify under the automatic pathway of (d)(3)(i) and would instead need to meet the FGE and NTL limits (added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium) specified for mixed products. The effective date of the rule is April 28, 2025 (as delayed by 90 FR 10592, Doc. 2025-03118). The compliance date is February 25, 2028, as stated in the final rule (89 FR 106064). Until that compliance date, you may continue to use the 'healthy' claim under the prior criteria, but by February 25, 2028, your product must meet the updated requirements or the claim must be removed.

response.answer: Your supplier is partially correct in a narrow technical sense but draws the wrong conclusion. The Red No. 3 order (Doc 2025-00830, 90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16) indeed sets no explicit 'compliance date' — it states only effective dates. However, the absence of a compliance date does not mean there is no hard deadline. It means the deadline IS the effective date itself. Once the effective date arrives, 21 CFR 74.303 is removed from the Code of Federal Regulations, and FD&C Red No. 3 is no longer a listed color additive for food use. After that date, any food containing Red No. 3 is adulterated under 21 U.S.C. 721(a). The operative deadline for food use is January 15, 2027 (for all provisions except amendatory instruction 4, which addresses ingested drugs and takes effect January 18, 2028). Per the timeline facts, this deadline is 'derived from the effective date' because no separate compliance date was stated (timeline entry: '2025-00830 sets no compliance date; deadline derived from the effective date stated by 2025-00830'). Note that an administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) was in effect from February 18, 2025 through August 5, 2026, but that stay has now ended and did not change any dates (timeline: 'dates_changed: false'). Therefore, the January 15, 2027 effective date remains the hard deadline for food-use inventory. Any colored inventory introduced into interstate commerce after that date would be adulterated. Your supplier's interpretation that 'no compliance date = no deadline' is incorrect.

response.answer: Your compliance memo's recorded date of January 15, 2025 is incorrect. The Red No. 3 revocation order (Document No. 2025-00830) was published in the Federal Register on January 16, 2025, at 90 FR 4628. This is confirmed by both the order itself (90 FR 4628) and the subsequent order lifting the administrative stay (91 FR 50475, published August 5, 2026), which repeatedly references 'the order that published in the Federal Register of January 16, 2025 (90 FR 4628).' The date January 15, 2027 is the effective date for the food-use provisions, not the publication date.
